name: PATRICK INDUSTRIES

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: Unlike LCII, Patrick is the ACQUIRER and the continuing registrant. Its price floats freely rather than being pinned to an exchange ratio, so a standalone reverse DCF on Patrick is not meaningless the way one on LCII was — it is a real market opinion about real cash flows. And if the deal breaks on antitrust, Patrick reverts to a standalone business generating $246-350M of free cash flow against a $2.3B market cap, which at a -2.8% implied growth rate would be genuinely cheap. Refusing may be discarding a real signal.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The Form S-4 joint proxy, which will carry pro-forma combined financials, the synergy estimate and the pro-forma capital structure; and the outcome of the refiled HSR waiting period. Those two documents together decide whether the standalone number means anything.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Neither is available — the S-4 has not been filed as of today, which is itself one of the closing conditions. What IS visible defeats the counter on its own terms: the counter's 'cheap on a standalone basis' rests on the -2.8% implied growth, and that figure is only striking against the +9.7% baseline, which I have shown is measured off the 2020 COVID trough. Measured against the 2022 peak, Patrick's revenue CAGR is negative. Strip the artifact and there is no standalone gap to preserve.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I could not assess the antitrust risk itself. A voluntary pull-and-refile is consistent with the agencies preparing a Second Request, but it is also routinely used to buy time for ordinary document production, and nothing in the 8-K distinguishes them. I also could not verify the pro-forma leverage: Patrick's extract shows $1,418.7M of debt against an interest expense of only $4.3M, an implied rate of 0.30% that cannot be right, so even the standalone balance sheet input is unreliable.

what_changed: 2026-06-30 8-K (items 1.01, 7.01): the Merger Agreement with LCI Industries at a 1.2440 exchange ratio, ~52/48 ownership, $94.2M reciprocal termination fees, conditioned on both shareholder votes, HSR clearance, an effective Form S-4 and Nasdaq listing of the new shares. 2026-09-10 8-K (item 8.01): both parties filed HSR on 2026-08-05; Patrick voluntarily withdrew its notification on 2026-09-04 and refiled on 2026-09-09, initiating a NEW waiting period. Q2 2026 (2026-07-30): net sales $1.04B, down less than 1%, with Marine, Powersports and Housing offsetting RV weakness; net income +34%. Quarterly dividend $0.47. The 90-day news store contains no mention of the merger at all — the most recent company item is dated 2026-08-26 — so the news layer gave no warning on the single most important fact about this name.
consensus_case: The price is not an opinion about standalone Patrick Industries. On 2026-06-30 Patrick signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger with LCI Industries: each LCI share converts into 1.2440 Patrick shares, legacy Patrick holders end with approximately 52% of the combined company and legacy LCI holders approximately 48%, the board splits six and six, and the outside date is 2027-03-30 with two three-month extensions. The market is therefore pricing a company whose share count is about to roughly double, whose capital structure and synergy set are not yet disclosed, and whose deal carries live antitrust risk. The -11.9% five-day and -15.1% twenty-one-day moves that won this opportunistic slot are most plausibly that risk repricing, not the RV cycle: on 2026-09-04 Patrick voluntarily WITHDREW its Hart-Scott-Rodino notification and refiled it on 2026-09-09, restarting the waiting period — the standard manoeuvre when the agencies are preparing a Second Request.
base_case_rationale: No standalone growth rate is supplied, because a standalone five-year DCF on Patrick is a valuation of a company that has contracted to stop existing in its present form. The share count against which any per-share fair value would be computed (32,118,264) is about to rise by roughly 31.6M shares, and neither the pro-forma capital structure nor the synergy guidance is public yet — the Form S-4 is not yet effective. Separately, the +114.4% gap that won the slot is a cycle artifact independent of the merger: the naive baseline of '+9.7% five-year revenue CAGR' is measured from 2020's COVID-trough revenue of $2,486.6M to 2025's $3,950.8M, on a company whose revenue actually PEAKED at $4,881.9M in 2022 and is still 19% below that peak. Applying a growth rate derived from the recovery off a pandemic trough to a company now in an RV downcycle is not a thesis in either direction.
key_risks: Pending all-stock merger of equals roughly doubles the share count; no per-share standalone valuation is meaningful
Live antitrust risk — HSR notification voluntarily withdrawn 2026-09-04 and refiled 2026-09-09, restarting the clock
The +114.4% gap and 87th-percentile rank derive from a baseline measured off 2020 COVID-trough revenue
RV wholesale shipments remain in a genuine downcycle underneath the deal
watch_for: Form S-4 / joint proxy filing with pro-forma financials and a synergy estimate
Expiration, termination or a Second Request under the refiled HSR waiting period
Either shareholder vote being scheduled, or any change in board recommendation triggering the $94.2M fee
Deal termination, which would restore a standalone valuation question
